name: GitHub REST API
description: Repositories, releases, issues, commits, contributors and code search across the largest public code corpus there is. Useful as a data source in its own right - measuring what people build, when projects die, how fast issues close - and as the delivery mechanism for a large share of the open datasets that live in git.

license.name: API metadata is usable under the GitHub terms; repository contents keep their own licences

access.auth_note: 60 requests/hour anonymous, 5,000/hour with any personal access token, even one with no scopes
access.rate_limit: the X-RateLimit-Remaining header is authoritative; search has its own much lower limit of 30/minute
access.pagination: Link header with rel="next"; per_page max 100

probes.description: Directory listing, which is how you discover files in a data repo
The listing route that does not truncate at 1,000

recipes.title: Is a data repo still maintained
recipes.code:
curl -s https://api.github.com/repos/OWNER/REPO | python3 -c "import json,sys;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print(d.get('pushed_at'), d.get('archived'), d.get('stargazers_count'))"
# a 404 here is the single fastest way to learn a dataset has been withdrawn

gotchas.trap: A deleted or renamed repository returns 404 with a generic message, identical to a private repo or a typo.
gotchas.fix: Search the API for the name before concluding it is gone - and record the finding, because dataset repos disappear.

gotchas.trap: Anonymous access is 60 requests/hour, which one loop exhausts instantly.
gotchas.fix: Any token, even scopeless, raises it to 5,000/hour.

gotchas.trap: The contents API silently ignores per_page and page for a directory and returns at most 1,000 entries. Paging through it hands you the same first 1,000 over and over, so a large data repo looks smaller than it is - the AWS open-data registry has ~1,200 dataset files and this route shows 1,000.
gotchas.fix: Use the git trees API: /repos/OWNER/REPO/git/trees/BRANCH?recursive=1 returns the whole tree in one response, with a truncated flag when it really is too large.
